requirements.statement: The address book lives in the INS frontend at /address-book, reached from an 'Address book' item in the service navigation, and that item is marked active (aria-current) on the list, view and delete pages. The navigation also has a 'Log out' link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the address book behind the service navigation; DR1's inc-062 ruling already placed the real book in the INS front door rather than the animals frontend.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS frontend serves the list at /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p4-001, repo-tests-p12-001), its navigation links to it and marks it active on the list, view and delete pages (trace-ins-fit-p2-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-007, trace-ins-fit-p3-069), the fit suite proves the links (repo-insfrontend-p4-101), the INS dashboard links across to it (repo-tests-p12-039), and the list is the service's signed-in landing page (repo-tests-p12-129). The navigation's Templates item belongs to the shared layout area.

requirements.statement: A signed-out user opening any address book page is sent to sign in and returned to the page they asked for; a user whose identity holds more than one organisation chooses one first, and a session with no organisation is refused.
requirements.why: The book belongs to an organisation, so every page needs a signed-in user and their organisation: an authentication constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: Signed-out requests redirect to sign-in with the requested path (trace-e2e-p15-010, trace-e2e-p15-011) and sign-in returns there (repo-tests-p12-128); a multi-organisation identity picks one (repo-tests-p12-130, repo-tests-p15-124); the list needs the session's organisation (repo-insfrontend-p4-003).

requirements.statement: Address book page titles read '<page heading> - Import notification service - GOV.UK': 'Address book - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the list, '<address name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the view page and 'Delete this address? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the delete page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every page with the GOV.UK suffix and a hyphen separator.
requirements.deltaNote: The pages set their titles to 'Address book', the address's name and 'Delete this address?' (repo-insfrontend-p4-004, repo-insfrontend-p6-004, repo-insfrontend-p6-070), and the last captured rendering appends ' | Import notification service' with a pipe separator and no GOV.UK suffix (trace-ins-fit-p2-008, trace-ins-fit-p2-037). No claim records the suffix changing.

requirements.statement: The list page's heading is 'Address book'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading; today agrees.
requirements.deltaNote: The list's h1 is 'Address book' (repo-insfrontend-p4-004, repo-tests-p12-002, trace-ins-fit-p2-009).

requirements.statement: Under the heading the list page shows, in large body text, 'Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's intro copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list's lead paragraph reads this (repo-insfrontend-p4-005, repo-tests-p12-003). The older captures that show 'Manage addresses used across import and export services.' predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The list page has an 'Add a new address' button (a link styled as a button) that starts the add-an-address flow, shown whatever the list holds, on every tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers adding from the list; the add flow's own path is the INS service's.
requirements.deltaNote: The button shows always, whichever tab is selected (repo-insfrontend-p4-006), and opens the address type step (repo-insfrontend-p4-007, repo-insfrontend-p4-103, repo-tests-p12-217), including on an empty book (repo-insfrontend-p4-133).

requirements.statement: On the list page the 'Add a new address' button comes directly under the intro, above the 'Filter addresses' panel and the category tabs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's order of the page's controls.
requirements.deltaNote: The list template renders the button before the filter disclosure and the tabs (repo-insfrontend-p4-006, repo-insfrontend-p4-009).

requirements.statement: Search and the Type filter sit inside a collapsible 'Filter addresses' disclosure with a chevron, collapsed when the list loads with no search or Type filter applied, so the search field is hidden until the user opens it. It is the GOV.UK details component, styled to match the design, so it opens and closes without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 hides the filter behind a disclosure; the 9 October afternoon ruling makes it the GOV.UK details component so it works without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: The filter is a GOV.UK details disclosure, 'Filter addresses', closed on load (repo-insfrontend-p4-009), and the fit and end-to-end suites prove it opens and closes with and without JavaScript (repo-insfrontend-p4-116, repo-tests-p12-010).

requirements.statement: The search field is labelled 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label.
requirements.deltaNote: The search input is labelled 'Search' (repo-insfrontend-p4-010, repo-tests-p12-007). The older captures labelled 'Search addresses' predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The search field's placeholder is 'Search by name, address or country', and it has no hint.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts this text in the field as a placeholder.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the same words are the field's hint, read as its accessible description, with no placeholder (repo-insfrontend-p4-011, repo-insfrontend-p4-117).

requirements.statement: The search field has an icon-only search button whose accessible name is 'Search'. It is a real submit button of the filter form, so pressing it, or pressing Enter in the search field, submits the form with or without JavaScript.
requirements.why: The design's icon button, made a real submit control so the page works without JavaScript (the 9 October afternoon ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: The button shows a magnifying-glass icon with the visually hidden text 'Search' (repo-insfrontend-p4-012), and a search submitted with it or with Enter works with JavaScript on or off (repo-insfrontend-p4-118, repo-tests-p12-011).

requirements.statement: Search matches the trimmed text, case-insensitively and anywhere inside a field, against an address's name, every address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode), the names of the countries containing the text and the Type column labels of the roles it holds; a multi-word search is matched as one phrase, taken literally, and a blank search is no search.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 searches 'by name, address or country' and over the type labels; the address book holds role codes and country codes, so the INS frontend widens the search with the matching roles and countries.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book matches q over the name and address lines as a literal phrase (repo-addressbook-p3-021 to repo-addressbook-p3-025), and the INS frontend adds the codes of matching countries and the roles whose labels match (repo-insfrontend-p4-018, repo-insfrontend-p4-019), proven by name, line, county, country and role label (repo-insfrontend-p4-121, repo-insfrontend-p4-130, repo-tests-p12-029 to repo-tests-p12-031).

requirements.statement: The address book's country filter takes one or more ISO alpha-2 codes, each trimmed and blank ones dropped, matched exactly against the stored code, organisation-scoped, leaving out deleted addresses, and combined with the search term and search roles by OR; an unrecognised code simply matches nothing.
requirements.why: The address book stores a country code, so a search 'by country' reaches it as the codes of the countries whose names match.
requirements.deltaNote: countryCode is repeatable, trimmed, exact and unvalidated, and ORs with q and searchRole (repo-addressbook-p3-027 to repo-addressbook-p3-030, repo-addressbook-p3-040).

requirements.statement: The address book filter is a GET form to the address book list carrying the selected tab, the search and the chosen Type, and the address book API filters the whole tab by the search and the Type and returns 8 a page. The parameters that carry the tab, the search and the Type, and the values the tab parameter takes, are the INS service's to name. Pressing the search button, or pressing Enter in the search field or on the Type select, submits the form; typing or changing the Type select submits nothing by itself. The page works fully without JavaScript, and no script re-requests the list as the user types. The same holds locally, in the stub, on the compose stack and in CDP.
requirements.why: The real book is paged on the server, so filtering must run there; the 9 October rulings keep the server-side filters and the GET form, and design dropped filtering as the user types.
requirements.deltaNote: The filter is a GET form carrying the tab in a hidden field (repo-insfrontend-p4-014), the list request sends the tab's roles, the term and the matched countries and roles (repo-insfrontend-p4-071), typing or choosing a Type without submitting changes nothing (repo-insfrontend-p4-122, repo-insfrontend-p4-128, repo-tests-p12-073), and it works with JavaScript off (repo-tests-p12-079).

requirements.statement: While a search or Type filter is active, the submitted list's results line counts the matches (for example 'Showing 1-2 of 2'), and pagination shows only when the matches run past one page of 8.
requirements.why: The count and the pages describe what the user is looking at, which after a search is the matches.
requirements.deltaNote: A search with two matches reads 'Showing 1-2 of 2' with no pagination, and eleven matches page at 8 (repo-insfrontend-p4-119, repo-insfrontend-p4-120, repo-tests-p12-076).

requirements.statement: The list is split into category tabs, in this order: 'Origin and Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Transporter'. The tabs are the Ministry of Justice sub navigation component, labelled 'Address types', each a link that loads the address book list on that tab, with the selected one marked as the current page. The query parameter that carries the tab, and its values, are the INS service's to name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups the book by category; the 9 October afternoon ruling draws the tabs as MoJ sub navigation so they work by link without JavaScript, and EUDPA-776 left three categories on main (c-499).
requirements.deltaNote: The list shows the three tabs in this order as an MoJ sub navigation of links labelled 'Address types', selected by the addressType parameter and working without JavaScript (repo-insfrontend-p4-024 to repo-insfrontend-p4-026, repo-insfrontend-p4-115, repo-tests-p12-148, repo-tests-p12-154).

requirements.statement: Each tab panel has its own heading: 'Origin and Consignor addresses', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer addresses' or 'Transporter addresses'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's panel headings.
requirements.deltaNote: Each panel has its h2 (repo-insfrontend-p4-029, repo-tests-p12-152).

requirements.statement: An address is listed on the one tab whose category holds the roles it has: Origin and Consignor holds place of origin and consignor; Destination, Consignee and Importer holds consignee, importer and place of destination. Because an address's roles all come from one group, it is never listed on more than one tab, and the list API can be asked for one category's addresses. How the address record holds its roles is the address book service's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category membership; the 5 November ruling keeps an address's roles in one group, so one record sits on one tab.
requirements.deltaNote: Each role belongs to one address type and each tab lists exactly its roles' addresses (repo-insfrontend-p4-088, repo-insfrontend-p4-111, repo-tests-p12-059), and roles of two groups are refused (repo-tests-p12-162).

requirements.statement: With no tab chosen in the request, or an unknown one, the list opens on the Origin and Consignor tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's default tab.
requirements.deltaNote: A missing or unknown addressType selects Origin and Consignor (repo-insfrontend-p4-027, repo-insfrontend-p4-110, repo-tests-p12-150).

requirements.statement: Each tab link goes to page 1 of that category, keeps the current search and drops the Type filter; the filter form carries the selected tab as a hidden field so filtering stays on the current tab, and the chosen Type stays selected after a search.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's tab and filter behaviour.
requirements.deltaNote: Following a tab keeps the term, goes to page 1 and resets the Type (repo-insfrontend-p4-028, repo-insfrontend-p4-129, repo-tests-p12-068); the form carries the tab hidden (repo-insfrontend-p4-014) and the Type stays chosen (repo-insfrontend-p4-016).

requirements.statement: The legacy category values origin-and-sender and destination-and-receiver are not accepted as aliases.
requirements.why: They exist only so the prototype's older design releases keep working; the real service never used those values, so there are no links to keep alive.

requirements.statement: The filter has a select labelled 'Type' whose first option is 'Select one' (empty value), then options for the current tab only: 'Place of Origin' and 'Consignor' on Origin and Consignor; 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Place of Destination' on Destination, Consignee and Importer. A Type value the tab does not offer is ignored.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Type filter options.
requirements.deltaNote: The Type select starts 'Select one' and offers each tab's own roles in this order (repo-insfrontend-p4-013, repo-insfrontend-p4-034, repo-insfrontend-p4-035, repo-tests-p12-072), and an option the tab does not offer is ignored (repo-insfrontend-p4-038).

requirements.statement: The Type filter keeps an address when one of the roles it holds equals the choice, and narrows within the search; the list API takes the roles and the tab so the filter runs over the whole category on the server, still organisation-scoped and without deleted addresses. How the record and the API carry roles is the address book service's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Type filter, run on the server because the real list is paged.
requirements.deltaNote: Choosing a Type lists only addresses holding that role, AND with the search, across the whole tab (repo-insfrontend-p4-021, repo-insfrontend-p4-039, repo-insfrontend-p4-127, repo-tests-p12-075).

requirements.statement: Above the table a results line reads 'Showing <start>-<end> of <total>'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's results line.
requirements.deltaNote: The list shows 'Showing {from}-{to} of {total}' (repo-insfrontend-p4-057, repo-tests-p12-012).

requirements.statement: When nothing matches, or the book or tab is empty, the list shows 'Showing 0 of 0' and the table's headings with no rows, with no empty-state or no-match message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 draws no empty-state message.
requirements.deltaNote: An empty book and a search with no matches both show 'Showing 0 of 0' and an empty table, with no message (repo-insfrontend-p4-058, repo-insfrontend-p4-059, repo-tests-p12-014). The older captures of 'You have no addresses yet.' predate the change (c-171).

requirements.statement: The list's filter holds the search field, the Type select and the search button and nothing else: a user clears a search by emptying the search field and submitting it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no Clear search link; nothing that overrides the prototype applies.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a 'Clear search' link shows above the table while a term is in force and returns to the tab's first page with no term, keeping the Type (repo-insfrontend-p4-022, repo-insfrontend-p4-023, repo-tests-p12-017); its Welsh is 'Clirio'r chwiliad' (repo-insfrontend-p4-092).

requirements.statement: On the Origin and Consignor and the Destination, Consignee and Importer tabs the table's columns are Name, Type, Address and Country, then an action column whose header 'Action' is visually hidden.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's table.
requirements.deltaNote: The address tabs' table has these columns (repo-insfrontend-p4-041, repo-tests-p12-018). The older captures with no Type column predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, then the hidden Action column, with no Country column. The Address cell ends with the transporter's country as its last line, 'Northern Ireland' for a commercial transporter; Approval number reads 'Not applicable' when there is none; and Type reads 'Commercial' or 'Private'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's transporter table; the 6 November ruling fixes a commercial transporter's country to Northern Ireland.
requirements.deltaNote: The Transporter table has these columns and cells (repo-insfrontend-p4-042, repo-insfrontend-p4-051 to repo-insfrontend-p4-054, repo-insfrontend-p4-131, repo-tests-p12-019).

requirements.statement: In the Name column a name of more than one word is shown on two lines: the first word, then the rest; a one-word name stays on one line.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's rendering of a listed name.
requirements.deltaNote: The Name cell breaks after the first word (repo-insfrontend-p4-043, repo-insfrontend-p4-109, repo-tests-p12-032).

requirements.statement: In the Address column every stored address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode) is shown on its own line, each but the last ending in a comma; blank lines are left out.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's address cell.
requirements.deltaNote: The Address cell shows each filled-in line on its own line (repo-insfrontend-p4-046, repo-tests-p12-033). The older captures that joined three lines into one predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The Country column shows the country's name, not its code, from the countries reference data, which always includes United Kingdom.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows country names; the address book stores codes.
requirements.deltaNote: The Country cell shows the name, or the stored code when the code is not in the reference data (repo-insfrontend-p4-047, repo-tests-p12-034).

requirements.statement: The Type column shows the labels of the roles the address holds, joined by ', ', in the order the address holds them, using the list's labels: 'Place of origin', 'Consignor', 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Place of destination'. These differ in case from the Type filter's options.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Type column labels.
requirements.deltaNote: The Type cell joins the five roles' column labels (repo-insfrontend-p4-044, repo-insfrontend-p4-045, repo-insfrontend-p4-113, repo-tests-p12-170).

requirements.statement: Each address row ends with a 'View' link to /address-book/{id}; its accessible name adds the address's name in visually hidden text ('View <name>'). Each transporter row's 'View' link opens that transporter's own page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's row action, with a distinct link purpose for screen reader users.
requirements.deltaNote: Address rows link to /address-book/{id} with the name hidden (repo-insfrontend-p4-049, repo-tests-p12-036), and transporter rows to the transporter's page (repo-insfrontend-p4-050).

requirements.statement: The address book list shows 8 addresses a page, asked for through the list API's page-size parameter, which runs from 1 to 100 and defaults to 25.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's 8 a page; the 5 and 25 November rulings keep the API's own bounds and default.
requirements.deltaNote: The list pages at 8 and sends pageSize (repo-insfrontend-p4-060, repo-insfrontend-p4-071, repo-insfrontend-p4-105, repo-tests-p12-020); the API takes 1 to 100, default 25 (repo-addressbook-p3-004).

requirements.statement: When there is more than one page, GOV.UK pagination shows below the table, with the current page marked, 'Previous' except on the first page and 'Next' except on the last; page links are the first page, the pages either side of the current one, the current page and the last page, with an ellipsis where pages are skipped. With one page there is no pagination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 pages the list with the GOV.UK pagination component; a real book can run to many pages, which the prototype's three-page book never shows (c-500).
requirements.deltaNote: Pagination shows only past one page, with Previous, Next and the first, neighbouring, current and last page numbers with ellipses (repo-insfrontend-p4-061, repo-insfrontend-p4-062, repo-tests-p12-022).

requirements.statement: Pagination links keep the category, search and Type filter, and add page only for pages after the first.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's pagination links.
requirements.deltaNote: Every pagination link keeps the tab, term and Type, and page only above 1 (repo-insfrontend-p4-063, repo-insfrontend-p4-064, repo-tests-p12-026).

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and one beyond the last page shows the last page's addresses.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's page handling.
requirements.deltaNote: Page 0 and 'abc' show page 1 and page 99 shows the last page (repo-insfrontend-p4-065, repo-insfrontend-p4-066, repo-insfrontend-p4-106, repo-insfrontend-p4-107).

requirements.statement: The list shows the newest address first, with a stable order from page to page.
requirements.why: A newly added address is the one a user looks for next.
requirements.deltaNote: The API orders newest first with ties by id, pages disjoint, no sort parameter (repo-addressbook-p3-013 to repo-addressbook-p3-015, repo-insfrontend-p4-080), proven end to end (repo-tests-p12-035).

requirements.statement: After an add, edit or delete the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner titled 'Success' above the heading, once: it is cleared when read, and it still shows when the list itself fails to load.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's confirmation of a change.
requirements.deltaNote: The list shows a waiting success message once in a 'Success' banner, also on its load-failure view (repo-insfrontend-p4-008, repo-insfrontend-p4-067-m1, repo-tests-p12-047).

requirements.statement: The success banner stays on the page until the user leaves or reloads it, and no script hides it on a timer.
requirements.why: WCAG 2.2.1 rules out a message that leaves on a timer (the 9 October afternoon ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: The banner is still showing ten seconds later and gone after a reload (repo-tests-p12-043).

requirements.statement: After a delete the list's success banner reads '<name> address deleted', with the address's name as the user entered it, or 'Address deleted' when the name is blank.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording; how the name is cased is c-367.
requirements.deltaNote: The banner reads '<name> address deleted', or 'Address deleted' with no name, set only when the delete lands on the list (repo-insfrontend-p6-081 to repo-insfrontend-p6-083, repo-tests-p12-044). The older captures reading '<name> deleted from your address book' predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The address book is stored by the address book service and belongs to the organisation: every user signed in to the same organisation sees the same addresses, and one user's additions and deletions show for the others.
requirements.why: Persistence and sharing are real constraints the prototype's session store cannot express (c-172).
requirements.deltaNote: The address book keeps each organisation's records and another user of the same organisation sees additions and deletions (repo-tests-p12-124, trace-e2e-p15-077, trace-e2e-p15-078).

requirements.statement: Address book additions, edits and deletions held only in the user's session, with no address book API behind them, and a list that shows the session's own additions ahead of seeded addresses.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-172: the real book is persisted and organisation-wide.

requirements.statement: No caller can list, read or delete another organisation's addresses: the path organisation must match the caller's organisation header exactly, and any miss, whether unknown or another organisation's, is the same 404, never 403; in the INS frontend another organisation's view link returns the user to their own address book without showing the name.
requirements.why: Tenant isolation, a real constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: A mismatched path organisation is a 404 before any handler runs, with the same body as an unknown id (repo-addressbook-p3-053, repo-addressbook-p3-065), and the INS view redirects home without the name (repo-insfrontend-p6-022, repo-tests-p12-125).

requirements.statement: Every address book API call must carry a well-formed Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header (1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens); a missing, blank or malformed one is refused with a 400 problem response with no errors map, before any handler runs, and a new address is stamped with that organisation. Requests outside /organisation/, such as /health, are not checked.
requirements.why: The header is the address book's sole tenant key.
requirements.deltaNote: IdentityHeaderFilter refuses a missing, blank or malformed header with a 400 problem (repo-addressbook-p3-050 to repo-addressbook-p3-052) and stamps the organisation on create (repo-addressbook-p3-067).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend calls the address book server-side under /organisation/{orgId}/addresses with the signed-in session's organisation in the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, a JSON content type and the trace id, and refuses to call it without an organisation; a list answer that is not OK is raised as a failure.
requirements.why: The frontend is the trusted hop that sets the organisation.
requirements.deltaNote: The client builds the org-scoped URL and headers and refuses without an organisation (repo-insfrontend-p4-070, repo-insfrontend-p4-073, repo-insfrontend-p4-073-m1).

requirements.statement: The address book's trust boundary outside the service: stripping a client-sent organisation header, setting it from the verified session, CDP network policy, and the service's own resource-server authentication.
requirements.why: Platform and deployment controls the Design Release 2.1 programme does not change; it goes to the report as a standing risk nothing in the repo proves.

requirements.statement: The address book service logs each request with the caller's organisation id and no address personal data, logs list requests with their filters but never the search term itself, and logs each header refusal and cross-organisation miss once at warn or info; the INS frontend logs list, view and delete failures with the organisation and ids.
requirements.why: Operability without leaking personal data.
requirements.deltaNote: The list logs only whether q was present (repo-addressbook-p3-048), the organisation id sits in the logging context with no field values (repo-addressbook-p3-058), and the INS frontend logs its failures (repo-insfrontend-p4-068, repo-insfrontend-p6-024).

requirements.statement: The list API (GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses) returns a camelCase page object with items, page, pageSize, totalItems and totalPages, holds only live addresses, answers a page beyond the last with no items and the real totals, lists every live address when given no filter, and answers errors as application/problem+json.
requirements.why: The contract the INS frontend's list, results line and pagination read.
requirements.deltaNote: AddressPageResponse carries these fields over live addresses only (repo-addressbook-p3-009 to repo-addressbook-p3-012, repo-addressbook-p3-017), and the frontend reads them (repo-insfrontend-p4-072).

requirements.statement: Reading one address by id returns it with every stored field, including a deleted one with deleted true; only that tells a caller the address was deleted, and a 404 means unknown or not this organisation's.
requirements.why: Notifications hold address copies, and a tombstone must still resolve by id.
requirements.deltaNote: get-address fetches tombstones too and answers 404 for unknown or out-of-scope ids (repo-addressbook-p5-023, trace-e2e-p15-081).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address removes it from the list and search for everyone in the organisation but keeps it as a tombstone (deleted, name intact, readable by id); delete answers 204, is idempotent, cannot be undone, and is reached in the interface only through the delete confirmation page.
requirements.why: A notification that references a deleted address must not dangle.
requirements.deltaNote: DELETE soft-deletes, answers 204 idempotently and keeps the record readable (repo-addressbook-p5-008, repo-addressbook-p5-025, trace-e2e-p15-075); search skips tombstones (repo-addressbook-p3-018, repo-tests-p12-046).

requirements.statement: The address view page is at /address-book/{id}, headed with the address's name, and can be opened directly by its URL.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's view page.
requirements.deltaNote: GET /address-book/{id} renders the name as its h1 (repo-insfrontend-p6-001, repo-insfrontend-p6-003) and opens directly (trace-ins-fit-p2-050).

requirements.statement: The view page's summary list always shows, in this order, 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Town or city', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Country' (as a name), 'Email address' and 'Phone number', each value trimmed.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's view page rows.
requirements.deltaNote: The rows and their order are already right, but the first row's label is the form field's 'Name or organisation' (repo-insfrontend-p6-006), where the design reads 'Name or organisation name'; the last capture still showed 'Name or organisation name' (trace-ins-fit-p2-039).

requirements.statement: The view page shows 'Address line 2 (optional)' after Address line 1, and the county row after Town or city, only when they have a value.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves empty optional rows out.
requirements.deltaNote: An optional field with no value has no row (repo-insfrontend-p6-007, repo-insfrontend-p6-009). The older capture with blank optional rows predates the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The view page's county row is labelled 'County (optional)'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label, and the 14 October ruling keeps County on every address page.
requirements.deltaNote: The row is labelled 'County (optional)' (repo-insfrontend-p6-006, repo-insfrontend-p6-009). The older capture with a bare 'County' predates the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The view page's last summary row, 'Address can be used for', lists each role the address holds, one per line, worded as the roles question words them ('Place of origin', 'Consignor', 'Consignee', 'Importer', 'Place of destination'). The summary rows have no Change links: the whole address is changed through the Edit button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows on the view page what an address can be used for.
requirements.deltaNote: The view page shows no row for the address's roles (repo-insfrontend-p6-030); it already has no Change links (repo-insfrontend-p6-029, trace-ins-fit-p2-043).

requirements.statement: The view page's 'Edit' button, to /address-book/{id}/edit, is a secondary button, beside the Delete button in a button group.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's view page actions.
requirements.deltaNote: The Edit button is styled secondary (repo-insfrontend-p6-012) and sits with Delete in a GOV.UK button group (trace-ins-fit-p2-046).

requirements.statement: The view page has a red warning 'Delete' button to /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's view page actions.
requirements.deltaNote: The Delete button is a warning button to the delete page (repo-insfrontend-p6-013).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the view page's Back link goes to the address book list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Back link.
requirements.deltaNote: Back goes to the list when there is no return (repo-insfrontend-p6-014).

requirements.statement: The view and delete pages honour a return query: the view page's Back link goes to it, its Edit and Delete links carry it on, the delete page's Back and 'No, cancel' carry it to the view page, and after a delete the user goes to it unless it is one of the deleted address's own pages, when they go to the list. A return is honoured when it starts with a single / (an INS page), or when it is an absolute URL whose origin exactly equals the configured animals frontend origin, so a user who opened the address from a journey page of either animals set (live-animals or germinal-products, both in the animals frontend) goes back to it; anything else falls back to the list (view page) or the view page (delete page). A return that is the address book list itself is not carried onto the links. The return parameter's name is the INS service's to choose. Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP the allowed origin is each environment's animals frontend base URL, taken from the INS frontend's own configuration; in the INS stub mode only same-origin paths are honoured.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the user back to where they opened the address from; the animals frontend is on another origin, a cross-service constraint that extends the prototype's single-/ rule to that one origin and never to any origin (c-170).
requirements.deltaNote: An INS return is already honoured throughout: Back follows it, Edit and Delete carry it, the delete page's Back and 'No, cancel' carry it, a delete lands on it and one naming the address's own pages falls back to the list (repo-insfrontend-p6-015, repo-insfrontend-p6-016, repo-insfrontend-p6-079, repo-insfrontend-p6-084, repo-insfrontend-p6-085); the stub ignores an animals return (repo-insfrontend-p6-018). A return on another origin is ignored everywhere (c-170), so nothing yet honours an absolute animals frontend return.

requirements.statement: Opening the view page for an id that is not a live address in the organisation's book (unknown, malformed, another organisation's or deleted) sends the user to the view page's back link (the return path or the list) rather than a 404 page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 redirects to the back link when no address has the id.
requirements.deltaNote: Unknown, malformed, other-organisation and deleted ids redirect to the list or the honoured return (repo-insfrontend-p6-019 to repo-insfrontend-p6-023).

requirements.statement: Opening the delete page for an id that is not a live address in the book redirects to the return path or the list; posting a delete for such an id, or for one already deleted, changes nothing, shows no banner and redirects as a delete would.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete page guards.
requirements.deltaNote: Unknown and malformed ids redirect, a stale delete deletes nothing and shows no banner, and a not-found during delete redirects quietly (repo-insfrontend-p6-087 to repo-insfrontend-p6-091).

requirements.statement: The address view page showing addresses found outside the book (a notification's consignment, contact or transporter addresses), without Edit or Delete.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-173: those addresses are copies held by the notification service, not the address book, so the INS view page reads the book only.

requirements.statement: When the address book service fails unexpectedly, the list answers 500 with the shared recoverable error banner and no tabs, results line, table or pagination, while its heading, intro, add button and filter still show; the view and delete pages respond with the service error page; when the countries reference data is unavailable the list hands the failure to the service's generic error handling; each failure is logged.
requirements.why: A real cross-service failure the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The list's load-failure view and the view and delete pages' error responses are built (repo-insfrontend-p4-067, repo-insfrontend-p6-025, repo-insfrontend-p6-092).

requirements.statement: The view and delete pages render in the two-thirds column with a large heading; every address book page keeps the skip link, the GOV.UK header and the standard GOV.UK footer, and is built from GOV.UK Frontend components.
requirements.why: Today's layout; Design Release 2.1's custom page classes are styling of GOV.UK components, not a different layout.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p2-038 and trace-ins-fit-p3-070 show the two-thirds column, trace-ins-fit-p2-002-m1 and trace-ins-fit-p2-002-m2 the skip link and footer.

requirements.statement: The list, view and delete pages have no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.0 A/AA, 2.1 A/AA and 2.2 AA after the changes, on every tab, with the filter open and with a Type chosen.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a real constraint the service must meet.
requirements.deltaNote: Fit tests prove each page free of serious or critical axe violations (repo-insfrontend-p4-104, repo-insfrontend-p6-026, repo-insfrontend-p6-093).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation is served by GET and POST at /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete page; a confirmation stays a page.
requirements.deltaNote: GET and POST /address-book/{id}/delete are served (repo-insfrontend-p6-069).

requirements.statement: The delete page's heading is 'Delete this address?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading.
requirements.deltaNote: The h1 is 'Delete this address?' (repo-insfrontend-p6-070, repo-tests-p15-118). The older captures headed 'Delete address' predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The delete page shows a summary list with one row, 'Address', holding the name, each address line and the country name on separate lines, blank lines left out, and never the email or phone; with none of those it shows 'Not applicable'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete summary.
requirements.deltaNote: The one-row 'Address' summary and its 'Not applicable' fallback are built (repo-insfrontend-p6-071, repo-insfrontend-p6-072).

requirements.statement: Below the Address summary the delete page's only text is its warning line; it has no separate sentence asking the user to confirm the delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete page has the inset, the summary and the warning, and nothing else.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page also says 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.' (repo-insfrontend-p6-073, repo-tests-p15-118).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it warns 'Deletions are permanent and you cannot undo this.' (repo-insfrontend-p6-074, repo-tests-p15-118).

requirements.statement: The delete page's confirm button is a red warning button reading 'Yes, delete'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button.
requirements.deltaNote: A warning 'Yes, delete' submits the form (repo-insfrontend-p6-075). The older captures of 'Yes, delete this address' predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: Beside the confirm button the delete page has a 'No, cancel' link to the address's view page, deleting nothing and showing no banner.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's cancel.
requirements.deltaNote: 'No, cancel' is a link to the view page that deletes nothing (repo-insfrontend-p6-076, repo-insfrontend-p6-077, repo-tests-p12-045). The older captures of a secondary Cancel submit button predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the delete page's Back link goes to the address's view page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Back link.
requirements.deltaNote: Back goes to the view page (repo-insfrontend-p6-078).

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete deletes the address through the address book service and, with no return path, lands on the list, which shows no row for that address and counts one fewer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete outcome.
requirements.deltaNote: Confirming deletes through the service and lands on the list without the address (repo-insfrontend-p6-080, repo-insfrontend-p6-081).

requirements.statement: The delete form is protected by a CSRF token, posts nothing else, posts to its own URL and turns off browser validation.
requirements.why: Every state change is a protected form post.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete form posts only the CSRF crumb with novalidate (repo-insfrontend-p6-067, repo-insfrontend-p6-068, trace-ins-fit-p3-068).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address makes no check on whether a notification uses it and shows no in-use warning.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds no such check, and notifications hold their own copies of addresses.
requirements.deltaNote: No delete path checks for use on a notification (trace-ins-fit-p3-067).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend's in-memory address book stub behaves like the real list: 8 a page, filtering by search, tab and role, newest first, refusing an address with no roles or roles from two groups, and soft-deleting so a deleted address leaves the list and its view page redirects.
requirements.why: The fit suite runs against the stub, so it must exercise the list the design asks for rather than an unfiltered one.
requirements.deltaNote: The stub matches the term, countries and roles (repo-insfrontend-p4-020, repo-insfrontend-p4-078), lists the newest first (repo-insfrontend-p4-079), leaves deleted addresses out (repo-insfrontend-p4-077), refuses bad roles (repo-insfrontend-p4-084), and the fit suite proves 8 a page and a deleted address's redirect against it (repo-insfrontend-p4-105, repo-insfrontend-p6-023).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed English string on the list, view and delete pages has a Welsh counterpart, kept marked as an unreviewed machine draft until it has Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The INS frontend carries Welsh copy for every address book string; leaving the old Welsh would show users a different page in Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: Welsh exists for today's strings, tabs and types included, marked as a machine draft (repo-insfrontend-p4-091 to repo-insfrontend-p4-099, repo-insfrontend-p6-094 to repo-insfrontend-p6-099), but it renders the hint as 'Chwilio yn ôl enw, cyfeiriad neu wlad', keeps 'Clirio'r chwiliad', and has the old delete wording 'Cadarnhewch eich bod am ddileu'r cyfeiriad hwn.' and 'Mae dileadau'n barhaol ac ni allwch ddadwneud hyn.'; there is no Welsh for the delete inset, the view page's inset or its 'Address can be used for' row, and no fit test covers the view or delete pages in Welsh (repo-insfrontend-p6-100).

requirements.statement: The tests repo's shared address book fixtures each carry one role the add flow offers, so they land on the right category tab and the journey parties still find them; the pre-run reconcile treats a missing or drifted role as drift, keeps exactly one live record per fixture name, and the tidy-up deletes only the suite's own run records, never fixtures or performance-test records, and never in production.
requirements.why: The suites read the tabbed list against a shared organisation's book.
requirements.deltaNote: Twelve fixtures each hold a single role (repo-tests-p12-164, repo-tests-p12-165) and seeding rewrites a drifted role (repo-tests-p12-115, repo-tests-p12-116); the tidy-up is scoped to run records (repo-tests-p12-119, repo-tests-p12-120).

requirements.statement: End-to-end specs reach the address book's view and delete pages through its own links (list, category tab, search, View, Delete, 'No, cancel', 'Yes, delete'), and cover the empty and no-match state.
requirements.why: The behaviour is proven the way a user meets it.
requirements.deltaNote: The suite reaches a tab, searches, follows View and the delete and cancel controls (repo-tests-p12-036, repo-tests-p12-045, repo-tests-p12-141) and proves the no-match state (repo-tests-p12-014).

requirements.statement: The prototype's seeded demonstration addresses (its farms, transporters, three Defra branches, multi-type entries and padding copies), their slug ids, and its transporter country read off the end of a free-text address.
requirements.why: Demonstration data: the real book holds each organisation's own records, with generated ids and a stored country code.

requirements.statement: DR1's own address book screens and the animals frontend's navigation into them.
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements (the ruling), and inc-062 struck DR1's address book screens; Design Release 2.1 governs the INS book's design.

requirements.statement: Closing the test gaps today's suites leave on the address book: no fit test proves the list's load-failure view, the banner, the View links, the 'Not applicable' approval number, the Previous link or the ellipses; no end-to-end test proves the Previous link, a transporter row's action, the Private filter, the roles refusal's wording, a status code for another organisation's address, or the Consignee and Place of destination filters through the list; no fit test covers the view or delete pages in Welsh.
requirements.why: Coverage gaps in behaviour this programme does not change; they go to the report. Each requirement that changes one of these behaviours carries its own proof.

requirements.statement: The address book list, view and delete pages show the service's Alpha phase banner, 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.', with its feedback link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the Alpha banner on every address book page, and the INS layout already carries it.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS shared layout already renders an Alpha phase banner with that text and an email feedback link on every page (trade-imports-ins-frontend src/server/app/shared/layout.njk and copy.en.js phaseBanner, read at an earlier reconcile; no claim in this area's working set records it).

requirements.statement: The roles an address can hold read, in order, with these hints: 'Place of Origin' ('The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain'), 'Consignor' ('This is the sender of the consignment.'), 'Consignee' ('This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported.'), 'Importer' ('This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed.') and 'Place of Destination' ('This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address.').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording for the roles an address can hold, which also names the categories the list's tabs and Type filter group by; the choice itself is made on the add-and-edit area's roles step.
requirements.deltaNote: The five roles exist (repo-insfrontend-p4-087, repo-tests-p12-158) and the forms word them in sentence case, 'Place of origin' and 'Place of destination', grouped per address type (repo-tests-p12-156, repo-tests-p12-209), under the question hint 'Select where this address can be used' (repo-tests-p12-198); no claim records a hint against any role.

requirements.statement: The INS address book offers everything the k6 performance suite reads from it: the list at /address-book with the heading 'Address book', reached after signing in at the INS home; each tab by its addressType value, narrowed by role and searched by q; each row's link to /address-book/<id>; the add flow's address type form, the add-address form with its roles checkboxes, landing on the type's tab; the view page at /address-book/<id> showing the address's name; the edit page and its save back to the list; the delete confirmation at /address-book/<id>/delete whose form posts nothing but the CSRF token; a 200 landing after the delete with no link to the deleted address; and the results line marked data-testid 'address-book-results-label'.
requirements.why: The perftests repo is one of the programme's repos; changes to the address book must keep its scripts working.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS address book already answers each request the scripts make (repo-perftests-p1-008 to repo-perftests-p1-036, repo-perftests-p1-048), and the list carries the results label test id (repo-tests-p12-013).

requirements.statement: The k6 performance suite's address book scenarios work against a list split into category tabs: setup makes 'Perf Test Holding' findable under every role by searching each address type's tab narrowed to that role and adding it only where a role misses; each address-book session adds its address under Origin and Consignor, finds it by searching that tab, runs the worst-case search on that tab, and deletes what it added, so the suite leaves nothing behind in the book.
requirements.why: The perftests suite drives the tabbed list and must keep working as the list changes.
requirements.deltaNote: The scripts know the two role-backed address types and their roles (repo-perftests-p1-009, repo-perftests-p1-013, repo-perftests-p1-014), search tabs by addressType, role and q (repo-perftests-p1-010 to repo-perftests-p1-012), run setup per role (repo-perftests-p1-041, repo-perftests-p1-042) and delete what they add (repo-perftests-p1-037).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, the address book list re-requests itself as the user types in the search field or changes the Type select (debounced), and swaps in the table, the results line and the pagination without a full page load, with no apply button, enhancing the GET form that already works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design dropped it on 13 November: address search does not filter as the trader types, so there is nothing to build; the trader presses Search or Enter, which the list already does (req-1121, req-1122).
requirements.deltaNote: The list changes only when the filter form is submitted (repo-insfrontend-p4-122, repo-tests-p12-073).

requirements.statement: The address book list has a 'Transporter' tab, after 'Destination, Consignee and Importer', headed 'Transporter addresses', listing the organisation's transporter records rather than addresses, and the tab has Welsh copy.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has a Transporter category in the address book, and the address book is the service of record for transporters, so the tab is backed by the transporter records rather than by another address role.
requirements.deltaNote: The Transporter tab, its heading and its transporter rows are built (repo-insfrontend-p4-025, repo-insfrontend-p4-029, repo-insfrontend-p4-032, repo-tests-p12-058), with Welsh 'Cludydd' and 'Cyfeiriadau cludwyr' (repo-insfrontend-p4-094).

requirements.statement: On the Transporter tab the Type filter offers 'Select one', 'Commercial' and 'Private', and keeps a transporter whose type equals the choice, filtered on the server over the whole tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's transporter filter; a transporter holds a type, not roles (the 6 November ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: The Transporter tab's Type offers Commercial then Private and filters by type on the server, with and without JavaScript (repo-insfrontend-p4-036, repo-insfrontend-p4-040, repo-insfrontend-p4-132-m1, repo-tests-p12-089).

requirements.statement: The address type question offers 'Transporter' as its third option, after the two role groups, with the hint 'This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment.', and choosing it opens the transporter pages, which ask no roles.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers a Transporter address type with this hint, and the address book manages transporters, so the option has somewhere to lead.
requirements.deltaNote: The question offers Transporter last of its three options and choosing it leads to the transporter type question with no roles (repo-tests-p12-166, repo-tests-p12-196, repo-tests-p12-218), but its hint reads 'Private, Commercial' (repo-tests-p15-130).

requirements.statement: On the address book list the delete success banner shows the address's name with its first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased, for example 'Green valley farm address deleted'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sentence-cases the name, but lower-casing a name the user typed changes how their own data is shown, and the reason is not visible (c-367).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner shows the name as entered (repo-insfrontend-p6-081, repo-tests-p12-044).

requirements.statement: When the request carries a search or a Type, the address book list's 'Filter addresses' disclosure is open as the page loads, showing the search term and the type the results are filtered by.
requirements.why: Once the filter is submitted to the server, a collapsed disclosure would hide what the shown results rest on (c-368).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the disclosure is closed whenever the page loads (repo-insfrontend-p4-009).

requirements.statement: The delete page's Address row leaves out any line that repeats one already shown, ignoring case, and falls back to fields split out of a free-text address.
requirements.why: The prototype holds a seeded address as one free-text string whose last part is its country, so it has to drop the repeat and split the string; the real record holds separate lines and an ISO country code looked up to a name, so no line repeats another, and dropping a line the user typed would hide part of what is being deleted.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page lists every filled-in part of the record's address in its one row (repo-insfrontend-p6-071).

requirements.statement: The address book list groups and labels the address types 'consignor or exporter', 'exporter', 'contact' and 'packer'.
requirements.why: These four types exist only in the prototype's seeded demonstration data, which maps the service's own consignment and contact addresses into the book. No exporter role exists and none is to be created, the roles question does not offer these four and the prototype's own Type filter gives them no option, so the real book never holds one; building a category membership and a column label for each would be dead work.

requirements.statement: Search on the Transporter tab also matches a transporter's approval number, so a trader finds a transporter by the number on its approval.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search text for a transporter covers its approval number.
requirements.deltaNote: The Transporter tab's search also matches the country and the type label (repo-insfrontend-p4-055, repo-insfrontend-p4-056), but no claim records it matching the approval number.

requirements.statement: Every list of an organisation's addresses is served and shown a page at a time: the address book's list API takes a 1-based page number defaulting to 1 and a page size of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, refuses a page below 1, a size outside the bounds or a non-number with a 400 problem rather than clamping, and no caller is served an organisation's whole address book in one answer.
requirements.why: The 5 and 25 November rulings: organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses, so pagination is kept everywhere.
requirements.deltaNote: ListPaging takes page from 1 and pageSize 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, refusing out-of-range values (repo-addressbook-p3-002 to repo-addressbook-p3-006), and the INS list always sends both (repo-insfrontend-p4-071).

requirements.statement: The address book's list API takes the roles an address must hold, repeatable so that holding any one of them is enough, and separately the roles a search term is widened by, so an address holding one of those roles matches a text search even when its own text does not; repeated values collapse, an unknown role is a 400, an address with no roles never matches a role filter, and both filters run in the service, alongside the organisation scope and the live-addresses-only rule, before the page is cut.
requirements.why: The 5 and 25 November rulings: one request serves a whole tab, and paging the API cannot make the role filter wrong.
requirements.deltaNote: role and searchRole are repeatable, collapse repeats, refuse unknown values and run inside the organisation and ACTIVE scope (repo-addressbook-p3-031 to repo-addressbook-p3-041, repo-addressbook-p3-063), proven end to end (repo-tests-p12-083, repo-tests-p12-084).

requirements.statement: An address saved through the address book is found by the next search of the address book list straight away.
requirements.why: A user who has just saved an address looks for it next, and another user of the organisation should see it at once.
requirements.deltaNote: The service reads primaryPreferred, so a read straight after a write sees it (repo-addressbook-p3-092), and a just-added address is found first by the next search (repo-tests-p12-035).

requirements.statement: The address book list has a fourth tab, 'Branch', after 'Transporter', headed 'Branch addresses', listing the addresses holding the branch address role. Its Type filter offers 'Select one' and 'Branch Address', the Type column labels the role 'Branch', and the role reads 'Branch Address', after a divider, with the hint 'This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 draws a Branch category, and the rulings of 5 and 16 November describe a six-role vocabulary that includes the branch address; EUDPA-776 has since removed both the role and the tab from main with the consignment contact (c-499).
requirements.deltaNote: The list has no Branch tab and the address book refuses BRANCH_ADDRESS as an unknown role (repo-tests-p12-149, repo-tests-p12-161, repo-insfrontend-p4-025, repo-insfrontend-p4-085).

requirements.statement: When the view page is opened with an honoured return to a page outside the address book, such as the dashboard or a notification's journey page, it shows an inset under the heading reading 'You can only edit this address in the address book', and still shows the Edit and Delete buttons.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells a user who arrives from elsewhere that changes are made in the address book; the real service knows where the user came from by the honoured return.
requirements.deltaNote: The view page shows no inset; it already honours an INS return such as the dashboard for its Back link (repo-insfrontend-p6-015).

requirements.statement: The delete page shows an inset between its heading and the Address summary reading 'This will not remove the address from existing notifications.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's reassurance, and it is true of the real service: a notification holds its own copy of an address and a deleted address stays readable by id.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page goes from its heading straight to the summary, with no inset (repo-insfrontend-p6-070, repo-insfrontend-p6-071).

requirements.statement: The prototype's side effects of editing a seeded address in the session: the list's Address column, Name column and delete page still showing the old lines or name, an edited address moving category by its first ticked use, an edited branch's Type reading 'Branch address', a transporter's type becoming 'Transporter', and the view page splitting a free-text address into fields.
requirements.why: They come from the prototype holding seeded addresses as free text and merging edits over them in the session; the real book stores each field and saves the whole record, so none of them can happen, and an address's category is decided by its roles (c-172).

requirements.statement: The prototype's /design-release-2.1 mount for the address book, its rewriting of an unversioned /address-book return, and its shared views across design releases.
requirements.why: A design prototype decides look and feel, never URL paths or code structure; the real address book keeps its own paths (ruling of 9 October).

requirements.statement: Outside prod, the address book removes addresses, tombstones included, a configured number of days after they were created, so test data does not build up: expiry is off unless both its days and its index switch are set, a zero, negative or blank setting stops the service starting, and two safeguards keep it off in prod. Updating or deleting an address keeps its expiry date, which is never returned on the wire, and transporters expire the same way.
requirements.why: Today's operational behaviour of the address book; nothing in Design Release 2.1 changes it, and it keeps the shared test organisations' books small enough to page.
requirements.deltaNote: ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS, ADDRESS_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED and ENVIRONMENT drive the expiry with two prod safeguards (repo-addressbook-p3-071 to repo-addressbook-p3-077), and expired records are removed by the TTL index (repo-addressbook-p3-081, repo-addressbook-p3-084).

requirements.statement: The address book list is served by one compound index on organisation, status and creation time with no collection scan, and the service reads with primaryPreferred and writes with majority concern, over TLS, with a bounded connection pool.
requirements.why: Today's storage behaviour behind the list; nothing in Design Release 2.1 changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: The org_status_created index serves the list and the Mongo client is configured this way (repo-addressbook-p3-088, repo-addressbook-p3-089, repo-addressbook-p3-093 to repo-addressbook-p3-095).

conflicts.outcome: Search on the server, without JavaScript. The filter stays a GET form to the address book list carrying the tab, the search and the Type; the address book API filters a whole tab by the search term (over the widened fields) and the role and returns 8 a page. The search button is a real submit button, and pressing it or Enter submits the form; while filtering, the results line counts the matches and pagination shows only when the matches run past 8 (req-1118, req-1121, req-1122), all of which the INS frontend already does. Same locally, in the stub, on the compose stack and in CDP. Design's ruling of 13 November closes the question Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling opened: the list does not filter as the trader types, so the JavaScript half is dropped rather than deferred (req-2039). The prototype's mechanism of loading a category's every address into the page as JSON, filtering in the browser, pagination that ignores the filter and a search button that submits nothing is set aside: the real book is paged on the server, and every page must work without JavaScript. The prototype's icon-only look for the button is kept through the 9 October afternoon ruling's own claim. Sam's 9 October ruling leaves the names of the tab and search parameters to the INS service (c-253).

conflicts.outcome: The prototype's return query is adopted, shaped by the cross-origin constraint: INS honours a return that starts with a single / as an INS page, as the prototype does, and an absolute URL whose origin exactly equals the configured animals frontend origin, so a user who opens an address from an animals journey page goes back to it; anything else, protocol-relative returns included, falls back to the list (view page) or the view page (delete page). Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP the allowed origin is each environment's animals frontend base URL from the INS frontend's own configuration; in the INS stub mode only same-origin paths are honoured. Ignoring every other-origin return is replaced, and the single-/ half is already built (req-1167).
